f.title: Comply with the ADR reporting guidance and observe personal data privacy law
f.statement: Pharmaceutical industry should comply with the requirements set out in the guidance and should also observe the requirements of the Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance, Cap. 486, when reporting adverse drug reactions.
f.applicability: ADR reporting for all pharmaceutical products in Hong Kong

f.title: Apply the serious ADR definition when deciding reportability
f.statement: A serious adverse drug reaction is any untoward medical occurrence that at any dose results in death, is life threatening, requires inpatient hospitalisation or prolongs existing hospitalisation, results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity, is a congenital anomaly/birth defect, or is a medically important event or reaction.

f.title: Use the DH ADR Report Form or CIOMS form, one form per patient
f.statement: ADR reports can be made on the Department of Health Adverse Drug Reaction Report Form or the CIOMS form. A separate form should be used for each patient.

f.title: Complete the ADR report form and provide the items essential for causality assessment
f.statement: The form should be completed to the best of knowledge with as much information as possible. Items essential for causality assessment should be provided whenever possible: patient information (initials or reference number suffice), adverse reaction description (including date of onset and, for vaccines, reaction category), suspected and concomitant drug therapy or vaccine (product name, batch number particularly for biologicals and vaccines, dosage, route, start/stop dates, reason for use), interacting agents, treatment, outcome, sequelae, comments (allergies, hepatic/renal function, alcohol, smoking) and reporter details including contact information for follow-up.
f.clause: 4. What should be included in the Adverse Drug Reaction Report?
f.processes: Case processing & follow-up; ICSR quality control
